This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER

This first anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. has been filed on behalf of the applicant for grant of anticipatory bail as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.
564/2022 of Police Station- Kamla Nagar, District-Bhopal (MP) for commission of the offences punishable under Section 376(2)(N), 323/34,376(D) and 120-B of IPC.
As per the prosecution story, on 05.08.2022, prosecutrix lodged an F.I.R. alleging that she came into contact with Naveen Kumar Patel two years ago.
Almost 20 days ago, Naveen Kumar Patel came to her house, manhandled her and established physical relations.
She made a complaint of this incident to the Superintendent of Police, at this, Naveen Kumar Patel assured her that he will enter into the wedlock with her.
Thereafter, Naveen Kumar Patel took her to his home and stayed with her for a period from 11 to 17th.

It is further alleged that on 03.07.2022, Naveen Kumar Patel called her at Bhopal, attended her and took her from the Bus stand to his residence situated at Nehru Nagar,

sentences.text: At Bhopal, Naveen Kumar forcibly established physical relations with her and also beat her.
On 05.08.2022 at around 3.00 P.M. when she was sleeping, Naveen Kumar Patel asked her to open the door for his friends if they come there.
At around 3.00 P.M., one of his friend, who introduced himself as Aakash, came and forcibly established physical relations with her and went away.
After sometime, one another friend of Naveen reached there, he too ravished her.
Thereafter, Naveen came and beat her.
She made a call on 100 number and lodged an F.I.R.
In her statement under section 161 Cr.P.C and statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C, prosecutrix has supported her version given in the F.I.R. Investigation is still undergoing.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant, who is a police constable, has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has no criminal antecedents.
He has been falsely implicated only because he is Naveen's friend and room partner at Bhopal.

Learned counsel for applicant referring a alleged transcript of conversation filed by applicant alleged to have taken place between the prosecutrix and Aakash on 10.08.2022, has urged that in the conversation prosecutrix herself has admitted that she has falsely implicated the present applicant.

It is also the contention of the learned counsel that after getting information about registration of false F.I.R he himself had made a complaint to D.G.P and other senior officers of the police that on the alleged date of incident i.e 5.08.2022, prosecutrix was not present at Bhopal as the mobile location of the prosecutrix was found at Rehli.

It is also the contention of learned counsel that prosecutrix is in habit of lodging false F.I.R as she has made one other F.I.R for offences under section 498-A and 323 of IPC against Naveen Kumar Patel and prior to that also, she had made one complaint against one Aakash.
The entire police story is cooked-up and manufactured.
On the aforesaid pretext, it has been prayed that applicant be released on anticipatory bail.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant and submitted that a named F.I.R has been lodged against the present applicant.
Even in her statement recorded under section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C prosecutrix has made specific allegations against the present applicant.
The present applicant is friend and room partner of Naveen Kumar Patel at Bhopal where incident has taken place.
Therefore, no question of false implication and misplaced identity arise.
Investigation is still undergoing.
Applicant is in police department, he may influence prosecution witnesses.
As such, he has prayed for rejection of the bail application.
On perusal of the F.I.R, it is revealed that a named F.I.R has been lodged about rape against the present applicant and two others on the very day of the incident.
In her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C before the learned JMFC, prosecutrix has been consistent and has specifically named the present applicant as one of the author of the crime.
As far as the argument regarding tower location and registration of some other F.I.R by the prosecutrix against Naveen is concerned that is a matter of defence and may be relevant at trial.
No defence can be considered at this stage when investigation is still undergoing.

Hence, having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of anticipatory bail.
